request: Add a slugify(text) function to word-tools. It turns a title into a URL-friendly slug. Rules: lower-case everything; letters with accents lose the accent (e-acute becomes e); every run of characters that are not letters or digits becomes a single hyphen; there is never a hyphen at the start or end; an empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty string; a non-string input throws a TypeError with a clear message. Export it from src/index.js, add automated tests that cover each rule, and add a short section to README.md.

spec.summary: word-tools is a small library of text helpers for programmers. This change adds slugify, which turns a title such as "Café Déjà Vu!" into a web-address-friendly form such as "cafe-deja-vu". It comes with automated tests for every rule and a short explanation in the README.

features.title: slugify(text) function, exported from src/index.js, with tests
features.story: As a developer using word-tools, I can call slugify(title) to get a lower-case, accent-free, hyphen-separated slug I can put in a URL.
acceptance: `import { slugify } from "./index.js"` (src/index.js) yields a function, and the existing `capitalize` export still works
slugify("Hello World") returns "hello-world"
slugify("HELLO") returns "hello"
slugify("Café Déjà Vu") returns "cafe-deja-vu"
slugify("Crème Brûlée") returns "creme-brulee"
slugify("Café") (e followed by a combining acute accent) returns "cafe"
slugify("Hello,   World!!") returns "hello-world"
slugify("a -- b") returns "a-b"
slugify("hello_world") returns "hello-world"
slugify("Top 10 Tips") returns "top-10-tips"
slugify("  --Hello World--  ") returns "hello-world" (no leading or trailing hyphen)
slugify("!!!") returns ""
slugify("") returns ""
slugify("   \t\n ") returns ""
slugify("Привет мир") returns "привет-мир" (non-Latin letters are kept as letters)
slugify(42), slugify(null), slugify(undefined) and slugify(["a"]) each throw a TypeError whose message is exactly "slugify expects a string"
`npm test` passes, including the existing capitalize tests

features.title: README section for slugify
features.story: As a developer reading the README, I can see what slugify does and an example of it.
acceptance: README.md contains a line that is exactly "## slugify(text)"
The "## slugify(text)" heading appears after the "## capitalize(word)" section and before the "## Tests" heading
The slugify section contains the text `slugify("Café Déjà Vu!")` and the text `"cafe-deja-vu"`
The slugify section mentions that a non-string input throws a TypeError
The existing "# word-tools", "## capitalize(word)" and "## Tests" headings are still present

assumptions: slugify lives in its own file, src/slugify.js, with its tests in src/slugify.test.js, the same layout capitalize uses. It is re-exported from src/index.js next to capitalize.
The error message for non-string input is exactly "slugify expects a string", matching the existing "capitalize expects a string" style.
Strings count as input; anything else (numbers, null, undefined, arrays, objects) throws. A String object (new String(...)) is not a string and throws too, matching capitalize.

Accents are removed by splitting letters into base letter plus accent marks (Unicode NFD) and dropping the marks. Letters that don't split this way, such as ß, æ or ø, are kept as they are rather than turned into hyphens.
"Letters or digits" means any Unicode letter or digit, so non-Latin text like Cyrillic or Greek is kept (lower-cased) rather than erased. Underscores and all punctuation count as separators.
A string made only of punctuation or symbols (for example "!!!") returns an empty string, since the rules leave nothing behind once the start and end hyphens are trimmed.
Nothing else is added: no maximum length, no custom separator option, no transliteration of non-Latin scripts to Latin letters, and no new dependencies.
spec.uiContract:
This is a library with no UI or HTTP endpoints. The contract is the module API, the files and the README.

Files:
- src/slugify.js: `export function slugify(text)` with a one-line JSDoc comment in the style of src/capitalize.js. No dependencies; use only built-in String methods and regular expressions (for example normalize("NFD"), /\p{M}/gu, /[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu).
- src/index.js: keep `export { capitalize } from "./capitalize.js";` and add `export { slugify } from "./slugify.js";`.
- src/slugify.test.js: uses `import { test } from "node:test"`, `import assert from "node:assert/strict"`, and imports `slugify` from "./index.js", matching src/capitalize.test.js. There is one or more test() per rule: lower-casing, accent removal, collapsing runs into one hyphen, no leading or trailing hyphen, empty or whitespace-only input, and TypeError.
- Tests run with `npm test` (node --test), which picks up src/**/*.test.js.

Behaviour of slugify(text):
1. If typeof text !== "string", throw new TypeError("slugify expects a string"). Tests check this with assert.throws(fn, { name: "TypeError", message: "slugify expects a string" }).
2. Lower-case the text, decompose it with NFD, and remove all combining marks (\p{M}).
3. Replace every run of one or more characters that are not Unicode letters (\p{L}) or digits (\p{N}) with a single "-".
4. Strip any leading and trailing "-".
5. Return the result. Empty or whitespace-only input returns "".

Reference examples (input → output):
"Hello World" → "hello-world"; "HELLO" → "hello"; "Café Déjà Vu" → "cafe-deja-vu"; "Café Déjà Vu!" → "cafe-deja-vu"; "Crème Brûlée" → "creme-brulee"; "Café" → "cafe"; "Hello,   World!!" → "hello-world"; "a -- b" → "a-b"; "hello_world" → "hello-world"; "Top 10 Tips" → "top-10-tips"; "  --Hello World--  " → "hello-world"; "!!!" → ""; "" → ""; "   \t\n " → ""; "Привет мир" → "привет-мир".

README.md: add a section headed exactly `## slugify(text)` between the `## capitalize(word)` section and `## Tests`. In one or two sentences in the existing style, describe the rules, give the example `slugify("Café Déjà Vu!")` returns `"cafe-deja-vu"`, and say that non-string input throws a TypeError. Leave the other sections unchanged.
